source.question: q-79724
source.value:
Given that ${y}_{1}(x)=\operatorname{sin}⁡x$ and ${y}_{2}(x)=\operatorname{cos}⁡x$ are solutions to a homogeneous, linear, second-order ODE, then according to the superposition principle which of the following must also be a solution to the equation?

- $y(x)=(\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡x)^{2}$
- $y(x)=x\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡x$
- $y(x)=\operatorname{sin}⁡x+\operatorname{cos}⁡x$

decisions.reason: Observed MA content supersedes the stored value
